hints: Focus on the reagents, hot concentrated NaOH in ethanol signals elimination of HX to form C=C, not substitution to form alcohols.
Count the halogens in J, with two Br and one Cl you can lose three molecules of HX, so three new C=C bonds form in addition to the one C=C already present.
Check which carbons can lose H, a C with no hydrogens next to a C-Br cannot form a double bond there, so use the unchanged gem-dimethyl group and the number of alkenes to narrow it down.
walkthrough:
**Identify the reaction type**

Hot concentrated NaOH in ethanol causes dehydrohalogenation. Each C-Br or C-Cl loses HX with a hydrogen from a neighbouring carbon to give a new C=C.

$$\text{R-CH}_2\text{-CHX-R + NaOH} \rightarrow \text{R-CH=CH-R + NaX + H}_2\text{O}$$

**Count how many eliminations occur**

Compound J is $\text{C}_{15}\text{H}_{23}\text{Br}_2\text{Cl}$ and already contains one exocyclic $\text{C=CH}_2$ bond. Excess reagent removes all three halogens as $2\text{HBr} + \text{HCl}$.

$$\text{C}_{15}\text{H}_{23}\text{Br}_2\text{Cl} - 3\text{HX} \rightarrow \text{C}_{15}\text{H}_{20}$$
This product must have the original alkene plus three new alkenes, so four C=C bonds in total.

**Use the unchanged carbon skeleton**

The $\text{C(CH}_3)_2$ group on the left ring has no halogen and no reaction there, so it must still appear as two methyls on the same carbon in X. This rules out any structure with only one methyl at that position.

**Place the new double bonds**

On the left ring, the C-Br is next to $\text{C(CH}_3)_2$ with no H on one side and $\text{CH}_2$ on the other side. The double bond can only form toward the $\text{CH}_2$ side. On the right ring, loss of both HBr and HCl must give two new ring C=C bonds, a diene. Only the structure with gem-dimethyl retained and a diene in the right ring fits all these points.

options.A: Shows two alkenes in the right ring which is correct for double elimination, but the left ring shows only one methyl where J has a gem-dimethyl $\text{C(CH}_3)_2$ group. That carbon has no halogen and cannot lose a methyl, so A cannot form from J.
options.B: Retains the gem-dimethyl group and the right-ring methyl and the exocyclic methylene. It shows one new C=C in the left ring in the only possible position away from the quaternary carbon, and two new C=C bonds in the right ring from loss of HBr and HCl, giving the expected $\text{C}_{15}\text{H}_{20}$ tetraene.
options.C: Has only one methyl at the left-ring quaternary centre, so it has lost a carbon substituent which elimination cannot do. It also shows only one new C=C in the right ring, meaning only one HX lost there instead of two.
options.D: Correctly retains the gem-dimethyl group, but the right ring shows only one C=C bond. With excess hot ethanolic NaOH both the Br and the Cl on that ring should be eliminated to give a diene, so D corresponds to incomplete elimination.
